title: Adapt parameter proposals using progress before success appears
hypothesis: Sequential parameter proposals guided by task progress can exploit weak structures more efficiently than independent local and global draws.

prediction.against: budget-matched independent parameter search on baseline61_gen0_cand1_a0 and baseline61_gen0_cand2_a1
prediction.rationale: This tests adaptive proposal generation, not the search-versus-imitation comparison of D-005 or candidate pooling of D-007; eight points would justify a larger exploration-lane replacement pilot.

code_changes: scripts/stage_f.py (adaptive-search: shared 8, control 16 independent L/G, treatment 2 adaptive batches of 8 from a Gaussian over top-3 elites in range units, sigma in [0.05, 0.5], 20% uniform; finalist by success then progress then index)

falsified_by: The upper 95% paired interval is below +0.08; an interval containing zero is inconclusive about improvement. A positive estimate on these two structures alone does not establish general lane replacement.

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00021, 'revise' with changes applied) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is budget-matched independent search (shared first 8 + 16 independent local/global draws); the metric is already adaptive minus independent

result.notes: Two frozen weak evolved structures x search seeds 3030/3031; 24 candidates per arm, the first 8 shared and cached; probe s3032 (5 cases), confirmation s3033 (50). Adaptive minus independent, placement level: +0.070 [+0.038, +0.102], 14/0/36. Cell level (n=4, not independent placements): mean +0.070 [-0.069, +0.209]. Gains come from baseline61_gen0_cand2_a1 (0.94 vs 0.76 at seed 3030; 0.10 vs 0.00 at 3031); on gen0_cand1_a0 both arms chose the same shared-batch candidate (0.68 and 0.42), so the arms are identical there. Absolute: 24-candidate rollout search lifts these zero-shot structures to 0.42-0.94 at two of four cells, far above R-008's 8-candidate search. The probe has only 5 cases, so finalist selection is noisy. 1100 episodes (800 probe + 300 confirmation), 0 LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: Adaptive minus independent is +0.070 at the placement level [+0.038, +0.102], 14/0/36: positive, but the mean is below the predicted +0.08 and the upper bound is above it, so neither supported nor refuted. At the cell level (n=4) the interval is [-0.069, +0.209]; both gains come from one structure (cand2_a1: +0.18, +0.10) and the other structure ties because both arms kept the same shared-batch candidate. Separately notable: 24-candidate rollout search lifted these zero-shot structures to 0.42-0.94 in three of four cells.
verdicts.next_experiment: A confirmation with more structures (fresh weak evolved candidates) and a larger probe would settle adaptive vs independent; more practically, 24-candidate rollout search is a cheap, strong rescue for weak zero-shot structures and could become the exploration lane's default treatment.

verdicts.reasoning: The named budget-matched independent-search control was measured; paired_success_difference was +0.070, below the predicted +0.080 [logs/research/adaptive_search_s3030/summary.json]. The placement-level 95% interval [+0.0378, +0.1022] spans the prediction threshold, so the point-estimate miss does not meet the predeclared refutation condition [logs/research/adaptive_search_s3030/summary.json]. The cell-level 95% interval [-0.0687, +0.2087] includes zero, leaving improvement across search replicates inconclusive [logs/research/adaptive_search_s3030/summary.json]. Gains were confined to baseline61_gen0_cand2_a1; baseline61_gen0_cand1_a0 tied under both search seeds and therefore provides no evidence of improvement [logs/research/adaptive_search_s3030/summary.json].
